title: Destination controls accounted for 27% of corrected cover-gap closure in 40 plant transplant contrasts
abstract: We split plant community gap closure into changes in warmed plots and destination controls. Forty TransPlant contrasts in 20 gradients gave a destination share of 27% for relative cover after a plot sampling correction (95% cluster bootstrap limits 5% to 76%). The raw estimate was 25%, with limits that included zero. Thus the positive cover component depends on sampling assumptions. Plot occurrence gave a destination share of 9% (-7% to 21%). Warmed occurrence closure exceeded ambient control closure by 0.401 units of initial spatial separation (0.308 to 0.513); the cover excess was uncertain. Moving references matter for cover but do not explain away occurrence convergence. This is an accounting partition, not a causal temperature effect. Short records, small plot samples, cross-group covariance and a selected mountain sample limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, checks and source retrieval instructions are included. External source records remain outside the publication.
